biology.microorganisms-recall.0004.all: remove waste (filter/clean water); aerate / maintain oxygen levels (also monitor temperature, limit stocking density)

biology.microorganisms-recall-multi.0004.a: filter/remove waste; aerate water to keep oxygen high

biology.molecules-data-graph.0004.a: volume increases with pH to an optimum around pH 8 then decreases at higher pH; quote values from graph
biology.molecules-data-graph.0004.b: pH 4 far from optimum; H+ ions disrupt bonds in enzyme so active site changes shape (denatures); fewer enzyme-substrate complexes form; pH 8 is optimum, active site fits substrate

biology.molecules-data-pct.0002.b: rate increases to optimum at 40 C as more kinetic energy, more collisions/ES complexes; above 40 C enzyme denatures, active site changes shape; at 70 C fully denatured, rate 0

biology.molecules-data-plot.0001.a: temp on x, rate on y labelled, linear scale, points plotted, smooth curve
biology.molecules-data-plot.0001.b: rate increases from 10 C to maximum 46.8 at 40 C, then decreases rapidly to 0 at 70 C

biology.molecules-data-read.0004.a: read from graph at pH 5 (cannot see)
biology.molecules-data-read.0004.b: difference between readings at pH 5 and 9 (cannot see)
biology.molecules-data-read.0004.c: pH 4 away from optimum; active site changes shape/denatured; substrate cannot fit, fewer ES complexes

biology.molecules-describe.0002.all: add biuret reagent (or sodium hydroxide then copper sulfate) to food sample in solution; purple/lilac colour indicates protein (stays blue if none)

biology.molecules-describe-multi.0008.b: starch: chain of many glucose molecules joined; protein: chain of amino acids joined together

biology.molecules-explain.0004.all: active site has a specific shape; only one substrate is complementary/fits to form enzyme-substrate complex

biology.molecules-explain-multi.0001.a: a protein that acts as a biological catalyst, speeding up reactions without being used up
biology.molecules-explain-multi.0001.b: Benedict's tests for reducing sugar not starch; orange shows reducing sugar (glucose); starch must be tested with iodine (blue-black)

biology.molecules-ext.0010.all: Plan: equal-size potato discs/same mass in H2O2 at same conc/volume; water baths at range of temps (e.g. 10-60 C), equilibrate; measure O2 volume (gas syringe/upturned cylinder) in fixed time; control pH via buffer, surface area; repeat and mean; plot rate vs temperature

biology.molecules-mcq-rev.0005.all: Turns blue-black in the presence of starch

biology.molecules-prac-method.0001.all: drops of iodine on spotting tile; same volumes/conc of amylase and starch equilibrated in water baths at several temps; mix, start timer; every 30 s add drop to iodine; record time until iodine stays orange-brown; control pH with buffer; repeat

biology.molecules-prac-plan.0001.all: Plan: range of 5 temps; same vol/conc of amylase and starch, buffer pH; sample every 30 s to iodine, time to no blue-black; repeats + mean; equilibrate before mixing

biology.molecules-prac-reliab.0003.a: to calculate a mean, identify anomalies, make results more reliable
biology.molecules-prac-reliab.0003.b: boiled (denatured) protease with milk, or water instead of protease; shows clearing is caused by enzyme

biology.molecules-prac-risk.0001.a: iodine is irritant/stains - wear goggles/gloves; hot water - care
biology.molecules-prac-risk.0001.b: test more frequently (e.g. every 10 s) / use colorimeter

biology.molecules-prac-step.0002.all: to keep the pH constant; so pH is a controlled variable and only temperature affects enzyme activity (enzyme activity depends on pH)

biology.molecules-prac-vars.0002.b: volume of oxygen produced (in a set time)
biology.molecules-prac-vars.0002.c: temperature; size/mass/surface area of potato discs; volume and concentration of hydrogen peroxide

biology.movement-data-graph.0001.a: as concentration increases, percentage change in mass decreases (from gain to loss); no change at ~0.4 mol dm-3
biology.movement-data-graph.0001.b: 0.0: water potential higher outside, water enters cells by osmosis, mass increases; 1.0: solution more concentrated, water leaves cells by osmosis through partially permeable membrane, mass decreases

biology.movement-data-pct.0002.b: 0.0: water moves into cells by osmosis from dilute solution, mass increases; 1.0: water moves out of cells by osmosis to more concentrated solution, mass decreases, through partially permeable membrane

biology.movement-data-plot.0002.a: conc on x, % change on y incl negative values, points plotted, smooth curve
biology.movement-data-plot.0002.b: % change in mass decreases as concentration increases; crosses zero ~0.4 mol dm-3

biology.movement-data-read.0003.c: larger cube has smaller surface area to volume ratio; acid has further distance to diffuse to centre; takes longer

biology.movement-describe.0001.all: diffusion is down a concentration gradient, active transport against it; diffusion passive, no energy, active transport needs energy from respiration (ATP); active transport needs carrier proteins

biology.movement-describe-multi.0005.b: cut equal potato cylinders, blot, weigh; place in range of sucrose concs for set time; blot and reweigh; calculate % change in mass; plot against conc, where line crosses x-axis (0% change) is the concentration
